historical_significance: 李世民（598-649），唐高祖李渊次子，唐朝第二位皇帝，史称唐太宗。他亲历隋末大动荡，16岁从军，18岁助父起兵长安，后以秦王身份统一全国，消灭薛举、刘武周、王世充、窦建德等割据势力。626年发动玄武门之变，逼父退位登基。在位23年（627-649），开创贞观之治——中国历史上最辉煌的盛世之一。他重用魏征等谏臣，推行三省六部制，完善科举，实施均田租庸调，开边疆设安西四镇，被尊为'天可汗'。晚年撰《帝范》总结治国经验。虎牢关之战以3500玄甲兵大破窦建德十万大军，是其军事生涯巅峰。
historical_significance_en: Li Shimin (598-649), second son of Emperor Gaozu of Tang, was the second emperor of the Tang Dynasty, historically known as Emperor Taizong. He experienced the Sui Dynasty's collapse firsthand, joining the army at 16 and aiding his father's founding of Chang'an at 18. As Prince of Qin, he unified China by defeating rival warlords Xue Ju, Liu Wuzhou, Wang Shichong, and Dou Jiande. In 626 he seized power through the Xuanwu Gate Incident, forcing his father's abdication. His 23-year reign (627-649) created the Zhenguan Golden Age—one of the most brilliant eras in Chinese history. He appointed Wei Zheng and other remonstrators, institutionalized the Three Departments and Six Ministries system, refined the civil examination system, implemented equal-field and corvée-tax reforms, established the Anxi Four Garrisons, and was honored as 'Heavenly Khan' by steppe peoples. In his later years he wrote 'Di Fan' to summarize his governance philosophy. His masterpiece military victory at the Battle of Hulao—3,500 black-armored cavalry routing Dou Jiande's 100,000-strong army—remains one of history's most celebrated demonstrations of concentrated force.

cross_references.relation_type: 权力伦理对照：开国 vs 守成
cross_references.description_zh: 李世民与毛泽东在权力获取方式上形成鲜明对比：李世民通过玄武门之变夺权（杀兄逼父），但登基后以纳谏、轻徭薄赋、任贤使能弥补合法性赤字；毛泽东通过长期革命战争取得政权，强调持续革命防止修正主义。二者都是极强能力型领袖，但李世民更注重制度约束自我，毛泽东更强调意识形态纯洁性。
cross_references.description_en: Li Shimin and Mao Zedong represent contrasting models of power ethics: Li seized power through the Xuanwu Gate Incident (killing his brother, forcing his father) but compensated for legitimacy deficit through remonstrance acceptance, light taxes, and merit-based appointments; Mao acquired power through prolonged revolutionary war and emphasized continuous revolution to prevent revisionism. Both were exceptionally capable leaders, but Li prioritized institutional self-constraint while Mao emphasized ideological purity.

cross_references.relation_type: 君民关系反向：水舟论 vs 天下主权
cross_references.description_zh: 李世民的'水能载舟亦能覆舟'与黄宗羲的'天下为主君为客'形成有趣的历史呼应：前者从统治术角度承认民本重要性（服务于政权稳定），后者从政治哲学角度颠覆君权合法性（人民是主体）。李世民的民本是工具性的，黄宗羲的民本是本体性的。
cross_references.description_en: Li Shimin's 'water can float or capsize the boat' and Huang Zongxi's 'Tianxia is principal, ruler is guest' form a fascinating historical echo: the former acknowledges popular importance from the ruler's perspective (serving regime stability), the latter subverts imperial legitimacy from a philosophical angle (the people are the subject). Li's populism is instrumental; Huang's is ontological.

cross_references.relation_type: 法治精神对照：宽简 vs 严刑
cross_references.description_zh: 李世民推行'用法务在宽简'的法治理念，与商鞅的'刑无等级'形成光谱两端：商鞅以严刑树立权威，李世民以宽简赢得人心。但二者都追求法律面前人人适用——区别在于商鞅的法律是君主意志的工具，李世民的法律是约束君主自身暴政的制度屏障。
cross_references.description_en: Li Shimin's advocacy of 'lenient and simple law' stands at the opposite end of the spectrum from Shang Yang's 'punishment without class distinction': Shang used severe penalties to establish authority, Li won hearts through leniency. Yet both pursued universal legal applicability—the difference being Shang's law was the ruler's instrument, while Li's law was an institutional barrier constraining the ruler's own tyranny.
